Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Conversation, family & daily routines

glad adjective

also be glad, I’m glad, I’m glad that, pleased, feel glad, feel happy

classical

Cic. Fam. 6.19.1: Maculam officiō fūnctum esse gaudeō.
Traupman 152, 155
Traupman 314

gaudeō, gaudēre, gāvīsus sum

verb, second conjugation, semi-deponent: with an accusative and infinitive, with quod, or with the ablative of the thing

be glad, be pleased

“I’m glad” is a verb in Latin, not an adjective: gaudeō tē vēnisse, I’m glad you came. It is the everyday word of Terence and of Cicero’s letters, often with vehementer, “very”.

Other words

  • laetor, laetārī, laetātus sum — be glad, rejoice

    verb, first conjugation, deponent: with quod, an accusative and infinitive, or the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 2.1.2: et laetor, quod absēns omnia cum maximā dignitāte es cōnsecūtus; Traupman 153; Traupman 314; Traupman 321

    Beside gaudeō in Cicero’s letters, of a joy that shows; it can also mean “rejoice” in a solemn sense (Lewis & Short).

  • laetus, laeta, laetum — glad, happy, cheerful

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Traupman 153: laetus, glad; Traupman 321

    The adjective, mostly of how someone looks or is (see happy); for “I’m glad that …” Latin uses the verb. Of crops and fields it means rich, flourishing (Lewis & Short).

  • volup est (mihi) — I’m glad, it pleases me

    phrase: the adverb volup with est, the person in the dative · also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 958; Ter. Hec. 857 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Old and comic, the opposite of aegrē est, “I’m sorry, it upsets me”.

Examples

  • Haud mūtō factum. — Gaudeō.

    I don’t regret it. — I’m glad.Ter. And. 40

  • Maculam officiō fūnctum esse gaudeō.

    I’m glad Macula has done his duty.Cic. Fam. 6.19.1

  • tē istīc invītum nōn esse vehementer gaudeō

    I’m very glad you don’t mind being thereCic. Fam. 7.13.2

  • nam quia vōs tranquillōs videō, gaudeō et volup est mihi.

    for since I see you calm, I’m glad and pleased.Plaut. Amph. 958

See also happy, I’m glad to hear it, I’m glad for you, I’m glad you’re back, with pleasure, joy, pleasure.
